analysis.d: THE ARCHIVE’S NAME FRAGMENTS INTO A PERSON. «alexanarch marx» resolves partly to ALEXANDER MARX — four cards for three different men of that name — because "Alexanarch" reads as "Alexander".
analysis.reading: A COMPOUND COLLISION ON THE ARCHIVE’S OWN NAME. The query returns six archive and authored cards, and then FOUR CARDS FOR THREE DIFFERENT ALEXANDER MARXES: the Jewish historian and librarian (1878, Elberfeld, AAJR president), a data scientist in the causality group at the Research Center for Trustworthy Data Science and Security, and a Google Scholar profile. The mechanism is not a shared word — it is the archive’s COINED NAME being read as a common given name. "Alexanarch" plus "marx" becomes "Alexander Marx". A name built to be unique fragments into a name that is not.
